[1/3] Plan: keep project-specific REUSE annotations when the main license identifier is unchanged

impact_assessment.why: aikit.py fix fold refreshes REUSE.toml with a blanket AGL-1.1 annotation and would silently erase the brand-asset all-rights-reserved split
impact_assessment.benefits: the fix command becomes idempotent for projects that add asset-specific or third-party annotations; fold keeps its brand licensing boundary
impact_assessment.risks: contract: write_reuse_metadata output changes only when the same identifier is already present with extra annotations; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: the existing file lock around the caller is unchanged; state: a preserved file may keep an older copyright notice until the license identifier changes
impact_assessment.mitigation: guard on both the identifier and a second [[annotations]] table; add failing-first coverage for preserve and replace paths; keep the license text copy refresh unchanged

checkpoints.description: [2/3] Added a same-identifier guard to write_reuse_metadata and a failing-first test tier; the fold brand annotation now survives a refresh

[1/3] Preserve the UI check date when the identifier is unchanged

impact_assessment.why: ui begin, verify and finish refresh the UI identifier and rewrite .aikit/project.json outside the bounded surface, so the next verify fails and records a strike.
impact_assessment.benefits: Guard commands stop dirtying project memory and a clean UI task records zero strikes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: project memory write behavior changes; dependency: none; concurrency: existing file lock remains; state: ui_checked_at may stay older while the identifier is unchanged
impact_assessment.mitigation: Only skip the write when every identity field matches; identity changes still stamp and write; a failing-first test pins date preservation.

Reforge stage 9: window 27, 7 commit(s), 19 file(s) reviewed (unreviewed), 0 finding(s), 0 repaired
[1/3] Harden Reforge dirty-target delivery and REUSE blanket matching

impact_assessment.why: Stage 9 found two defects: a direct fix-then-commit never records pre-existing dirty targets, and a REUSE refresh accepts a matching identifier from an asset annotation while the blanket annotation names another license.
impact_assessment.benefits: A later commit cannot publish another session's edit, and a same-identifier REUSE refresh always keeps the matching blanket annotation.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Reforge state gains dirty_targets in fix mode and REUSE refresh keeps fewer stale files; dependency: none; concurrency: existing locks remain; state: dirty_targets is additive
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first regression tests cover both paths; the fixes are small and use the existing state and lock modules.
